body:
EDIT: Turns out this was a bug. I couldn't reproduce and misunderstood the issue, thought it was purely a documentation issue. Sorry. 😊  

...

As well as interpolating transforms, the Fixed Timestep Interpolation (FTI / physics interpolation) can also interpolate properties (where coded in the engine).

Most of the properties of `Camera3D` are interpolated (`FOV`, `near plane`, `far plane`) so they can be changed smoothly at runtime like the camera transform, without causing glitches.

In the same way as transform, if you want an immediate change (when using FTI on a node), you need to call `reset_physics_interpolation()` after the change.

It's possible we could add this to documentation.

### Properties
If you think about it, a lot of properties on nodes could benefit from FTI, in addition to transform.

If you run a game with FTI at 10tps (as recommended in the documentation for testing), and change some properties (e.g. animation blends) you will currently get a glitch if you change them on the physics tick, and you would need to interpolate them manually to get smooth motion.

Longterm we would aim to interpolate more properties to make this easier for users.

There may come a point where we want to add individual control for only resetting specific properties .. but it hasn't come up as a problem yet, as only a few properties are currently implemented.

If a user sets their FOV to be 20, they should expect the FOV to be set to 20, especially when the inspector says the FOV is at 20, yet the game editor is lying to the user and its actually at ~24. The interpolation seems to be unclamped and severely under/overshooting its target. **A good solution would be to clamp to the intended value, although I believe it still undershoots.**

(Also, camera FOV being conflated with physics is obtuse and should be a separate setting, or removed altogether and just done by the user if it will lead to such drastic inaccuracies. Although this is a separate issue.)

> camera FOV being conflated with physics is obtuse

https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/physics/interpolation/physics_interpolation_introduction.html#fixed-timestep-interpolation

This is why I argued from the start against calling the FTI "physics interpolation", because it is nothing to do with physics (aside from being tied to physics ticks). I brought up again and again the potential for user confusion, but it was decided that "physics interpolation" was a more user friendly term. 🤷 

It is a kind of damned if you do, damned if you don't situation. Users brains can switch off with new jargon (FTI), but they can be confused in the long run by inaccurate terms (physics interpolation). This is the price we pay.

> If a user sets their FOV to be 20, they should expect the FOV to be set to 20

Exactly the same argument could be made for node position, scale, rotation, which are also interpolated in the same way though.

The paradigm for an FTI node is currently:
* Setting any property that is interpolated will result in interpolation _unless_ you call `reset_physics_interpolation()`

This works, even though there is a bit of a gotcha on first discovering how it works (as you are finding). We typically get a lot of issues where users discover a quirk (that might be historical for example, as in this case) and it isn't super intuitive, and blame the engine and say it is a bug etc. But in some cases it is simply a compromise that we have had to make so as to not break the engine for existing users.

The problem as far as providing a user facing method is that it has to be backward compatible, and easy to change non-interpolated game code to interpolated. We can't easily change existing function definitions (e.g. adding a default param), or duplicate every existing function with an e.g. `set_fov()` and `set_fov_interpolated()`.

The most minimal intervention to the API is to have the existing functions work with interpolation, then add the specific call to `reset_physics_interpolation()` for the specific case where you need an instantaneous change.

If you can think of alternative ways of providing this functionality to users, it would be welcome.

### Property Interpolation
From a glance at the code to remind myself, it works just by linear interpolation, with a current value and previous value, linearly interpolating between the two. As with transforms, the interpolated properties should only be set on physics ticks.

It's here if you want to take a look:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/core/templates/interpolated_property.h

You shouldn't get overshooting or undershooting, or need to clamp, but maybe there's something specific about your MRP that is causing problems (maybe it's the need to call only on physics ticks). If you want to see what is actually happening, I highly recommend changing your physics tick rate to a low value (say 5tps in your MRP).

https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/physics/interpolation/using_physics_interpolation.html#testing-and-debugging-tips

I'll try and add this to the docs (it's also possible we didn't add immediately to the docs just in case we changed it around a bit, sometimes we need user feedback to finalize things).

### Switching off per node
If you don't want to use FTI for a node, as you say you can switch it off on a per node basis and handle things yourself (this is actually recommended in many cases for `Cameras` especially with mouse look, see https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/physics/interpolation/advanced_physics_interpolation.html#cameras).

My problem is less so about FTI, and more about why this is being applied to the camera, because FTI needs a constant flow of values. **interpolated_property either needs to be made to not under/overshoot so it can just be set once, or entirely removed from use in camera_3d**. The user should not be expected to have to set the FOV, near plane, and/or far plane of the camera every SINGLE physics tick for the rest of the game if they want to change each of them just once.

> Exactly the same argument could be made for node position, scale, rotation, which are also interpolated in the same way though.

This is not the case, because these are not using interpolated_property.h, and so they do not have the same issues. The problem is the implementation in this header.

> You shouldn't get overshooting or undershooting, or need to clamp

That is what interpolated_property.h is currently doing, you can just read the the code to see that it's lerping without any clamps on line 71, and it stops lerping whenever pump is called, regardless of what the current value is set at. My MRP shows it over/overshooting by nearly 50% on default physics tick + 170hz monitor. The problem may be that 1. the lerp is unclamped and 2. pump() is stopping the interpolation too early before the desired value is reached. Apologies, I can't be more specific as I don't have experience in C++.

In my MRP I have it zoom the camera in using FOV bound to right mouse button, as a very common use case, lets say for binoculars, and its completely jank. I can't even think of a use case for this for the camera, who is going to be interpolating the FOV when bound to the physics tick? This is incredibly jarring as seen in the MRE and should instead be done tied to _process for it to be smooth, which can easily be done by the user.

As for the near/far plane, can you think of a use case where a user:
1. wants the near plane of the camera to be implicitly interpolated by the engine when they set it to a hard value
2. does not care if the resulting value under/overshoots, so the ACTUAL near plane can be off by nearly 50%, leading to z-fighting that occurs only sometimes, even when the inspector always shows the same number
3. The user cannot just easily tween it themselves

I personally think interpolated_property needs to be tweaked, or should just be removed altogether, as it seems it was designed to be reused but is only being used by camera_3d at the moment. The design of it is not suitable for FOV and near/far plane of the camera. It is only suitable for things that are expected to be set every tick. I apologize that I have no experience in C++ to provide a code solution for the former.

I'm also affected by this bug.

> In the same way as transform, if you want an immediate change (when using FTI on a node), you need to call reset_physics_interpolation() after the change.

This is not addressing the issue, transforms when assigned to outside of the physics loop will keep interpolating towards their assigned value, the camera FOV property won't.

The FOV once set, has it's effect "partially applied" considering the current interpolation factor, but it's not interpolated further, so the real visible effect on screen differs from the assigned value. We aren't talking about just "instantly", **the effective value NEVER reaches the assigned value unless the property is assigned to again, which is clearly a bug**.

**If I assign FOV = 90, I expect FOV to reach 90 eventually even if it's being interpolated, which currently doesn't happen.**

Attached is another MRP where that difference is more pronounced and includes some debug logs. If your interpolation factor is stuck on either 0 or 1 restart the project otherwise no effects will be visible.

[fov-bug-demo.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26239012/fov-bug-demo.zip)
Press 1, 2, 3, 4 to assign different FOVs. If the interpolation factor of the current frame is partial, you'll notice that you'll have to press each keybind TWICE to get the correct FOV.
And for anyone else running into this, the current workaround of calling `$Camera3D.reset_physics_interpolation()` after assigning new values to the property does work, but it's clearly a workaround.

Sorry about that, with the new MRP I can confirm there does seem to be a bug, maybe order of operations. I wasn't seeing it before because I dropped the tick rate to a low value (where it becomes very subtle), but this one shows up _more_ at high ticks.

I've created a 3.x MRP and am investigating. 👍
Have worked out the problem and a fix (see above). I'll double check it's the best fix, then port to 4.x. 👍
